# Disagreement Log — Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 52

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET (literal) | LOGOS (formal) | PNEUMA (dynamic)
**Total Disagreements:** 8

---

## Disagreement 1 — 52:1 "withered" vs. "dry" vs. "dead"

- **EMET:** "seemed to me to be withered"
- **LOGOS:** "appeared to me to be dry"
- **PNEUMA:** "all looked dead to me"
- **Greek:** *xēra...xēra* — dry, dried out, withered
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "appeared to me to be dry" (LOGOS). *Xēros* means dry/dried; "withered" suggests previous life; "dead" (PNEUMA) is an interpretive addition. "Dry" is most precise.

---

## Disagreement 2 — 52:1 "appear alike" vs. "look alike"

- **EMET:** "they all appeared alike"
- **LOGOS:** "they all looked alike"
- **PNEUMA:** "they were all identical in appearance"
- **Greek:** *homoiai hai panti* — alike to one another in every way
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "they all looked alike" (LOGOS). "Look alike" is more natural English for visual similarity.

---

## Disagreement 3 — 52:1 "those who live in this present age" vs. "those who dwell in this present age"

- **EMET:** "those who live in this present age"
- **LOGOS:** "those who dwell in this present age"
- **PNEUMA:** "the people living in the present age"
- **Greek:** *hoi en tō aiōni toutō katoikountes* — those dwelling/inhabiting in this age
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "those who dwell in this present age" (LOGOS). *Katoikeō* = to dwell/inhabit; "dwell" carries the residence nuance; PNEUMA loses this.

---

## Disagreement 4 — 52:2 "neither the righteous nor the sinners are visible" vs. "not distinguishable"

- **EMET:** "neither the righteous nor the sinners are visible in this present age"
- **LOGOS:** "neither the righteous nor sinners are distinguishable in this present age"
- **PNEUMA:** "you can't distinguish the righteous from the sinners"
- **Greek:** *ou phainontai...homoioi eisin* — are not apparent/visible...they are alike
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "neither the righteous nor sinners are distinguishable" (LOGOS). "Distinguishable" captures the identification problem better than "visible" — they are present but indistinguishable.

---

## Disagreement 5 — 52:2 "winter for the righteous" — all agree substantially

- **EMET:** "this age is winter for the righteous who live in it"
- **LOGOS:** "this present age is winter for the righteous who dwell in it"
- **PNEUMA:** "This present age is winter for the righteous who live in it"
- **Note:** Minor variation only.
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "this present age is winter for the righteous who dwell in it" (LOGOS). Consistent use of "dwell" for *katoikeō*.

---

## Disagreement 6 — 52:3 "dry and which are living" vs. "withered and which are alive"

- **EMET:** "which are dry and which are living"
- **LOGOS:** "which are withered and which are alive"
- **PNEUMA:** "which ones are dead and which are still alive"
- **Greek:** *xēra...zōsa* — dry/withered...living
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "which are withered and which are alive" (LOGOS). "Withered" vs "alive" is a sharper contrast than "dry vs living"; PNEUMA's "dead" goes beyond the Greek.

---

## Disagreement 7 — 52:3 "so also in this present age" — conjunction

- **EMET:** "so also in this present age"
- **LOGOS:** "so too in this present age"
- **PNEUMA:** "In the same way, in this present age"
- **Note:** Stylistic preference only.
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "so too in this present age" (LOGOS). "So too" is more elegant than "so also" or PNEUMA's full phrase.

---

## Disagreement 8 — 52:3 "neither the righteous are visible, nor the sinners" — word order

- **EMET:** "the righteous are not visible, nor the sinners"
- **LOGOS:** "neither the righteous nor the sinners are apparent"
- **PNEUMA:** "you can't identify who is righteous and who is a sinner"
- **Greek:** *ou phainetai ho dikaios oude ho hamartōlos* — neither the righteous nor the sinner is apparent
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "neither the righteous nor sinners are apparent" (LOGOS). The paired negation should be preserved; PNEUMA's active "you can't identify" shifts the perspective.

---

*End of disagreement log for Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 52.*
